# Configuration

Every setting is an environment variable. Where its value comes from:

- **The project's own settings**, for the variables marked *project setting*.
  They are kept in `~/.pragma/registry.json`, one set per project, and a
  project that has never set one has none. Opening a project sets each of them
  from there and clears whatever the shell held, so a value left over from
  another project cannot leak in. On Windows `pragma -Set <key> <value>`
  writes one; the steps a turn may take are asked by `/settings` everywhere.
- **The shell** the launcher was started from, for every other variable.
- **`.env`** in the repository root, for anything neither of those named.
  See [`.env.example`](../../.env.example).
- **The default** in the table.

The model server is the exception. Once `/configure` has written
`~/.pragma/endpoints.json`, the addresses, the sampling of each endpoint and
which role uses which are read from that file, and `LLM_BASE_URL`,
`LLM_API_KEY` and `DEFAULT_MODEL` are no longer read.

Most of these never need touching. The ones a new installation meets are in
the first two groups.

## The model server

Used until `/configure` writes its own file; the timeouts apply either way.

| Variable | Default | What it is | Read in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LLM_BASE_URL` | unset | Address of the OpenAI-compatible server, ending in `/v1`. *Project setting `Endpoint`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | unset | Key sent to that server. Local servers usually need none. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `DEFAULT_MODEL` | `llama3.2` | Model name sent in the request. A single-model server ignores it. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `PRAGMA_ENDPOINTS` | `~/.pragma/endpoints.json` | Another file to read the endpoint catalogue from. | [`core/endpoints.py`](../../core/endpoints.py) |
| `LLM_TIMEOUT` | `900` | Seconds before one model call is abandoned. *Project setting `Timeout`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `LLM_STREAM_CALLS` | `1` | `0` makes every call a blocking request, for a server whose streaming misbehaves. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `ENDPOINT_PROBE_TIMEOUT` | `1.0` | Seconds a connection may take before an endpoint counts as not connected. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `PRAGMA_NO_ENDPOINT_PROBE` | unset | `1` skips asking the server for its context window at start-up. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py), [`tools/pragma_launcher.py`](../../tools/pragma_launcher.py) |

## Sampling and reasoning

What a request sends when the endpoint's own table says nothing.

| Variable | Default | What it is | Read in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE` | `server` | Temperature of the agent's calls. `server` leaves it to the endpoint. *Project setting `Temperature`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `TOP_K` | unset | Sampling knob, sent only when set. *Project setting `TopK`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `TOP_P` | unset | Sampling knob, sent only when set. *Project setting `TopP`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `MIN_P` | unset | Sampling knob, sent only when set. *Project setting `MinP`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `SAMPLING_PROFILE` | the endpoint's own choice | `general` or `coding` picks that row of the endpoint's table; `server` sends nothing; `manual` sends the four variables above. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `SUMMARY_TEMPERATURE` | `0.2` | Temperature of the call that summarises older steps. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `AGENT_THINK` | the endpoint's own choice | `on` or `off` overrides, for one run, whether the model reasons before answering. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `MEMORY_THINK_BUDGET` | derived from `MEMORY_MAX_TOKENS` | Characters of reasoning after which a memory call is asked again without it. `0` removes the cap. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `RECALL_THINK_BUDGET` | `4000` | The same cap for the recall, which runs while you wait. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `MEMORY_SEED` | `42` | Seed sent with every memory call, so the same prompt gives the same answer. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |

## Budgets

How large a context, an answer and a single action may be.

| Variable | Default | What it is | Read in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CONTEXT_WINDOW` | asked of the server, else 65536 | The model's context window, in tokens. *Project setting `ContextWindow`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `MAX_TOKENS` | `16384` | Output budget of one agent reply. It has to hold a whole file being written. *Project setting `MaxTokens`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `SKILL_MAX_TOKENS` | same as `MAX_TOKENS` | Output budget of a model call made inside a skill. *Project setting `SkillMaxTokens`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `SKILL_MAX_TOKENS_RATIO` | `0` | Sets `SKILL_MAX_TOKENS` as a fraction of `MAX_TOKENS` instead. `0` is unset. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `MEMORY_MAX_TOKENS` | same as `SKILL_MAX_TOKENS` | Output budget of the memory faculties. *Project setting `MemoryMaxTokens`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `MAX_STEPS` | `15` | Steps a turn may take before the agent is told to conclude. A project opened from the launcher has its own number: 50, or what `/settings` was given. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `WRITE_FILE_SOFT_LIMIT` | `8000` | Bytes above which `write_file` advises smaller edits. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `WRITE_FILE_HARD_LIMIT` | twice `MAX_TOKENS`, at most 20000 | Bytes above which `write_file` refuses a single call. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `OBSERVATION_SOFT_LIMIT` | `12000` | Characters above which a tool's output is shortened in the history. `0` disables. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `PRAGMA_MD_MAX_CHARS` | `4000` | Characters of the workspace's `PRAGMA.md` that are passed to the agent. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |

## When the conversation outgrows the window

A batch run summarises its older steps; a conversation turns its older turns into memory.

| Variable | Default | What it is | Read in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `COMPRESS_TOKENS` | same as `CHAT_COMPACT_TOKENS` | Prompt tokens above which the agent summarises its older steps. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `MAX_MESSAGES` | `0` | Also summarise above this many messages. `0` counts nothing. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `MESSAGES_RECENT` | `6` | Most recent messages kept word for word when the rest is summarised. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `RECENT_MAX_CHARS` | a quarter of the window | Ceiling on those recent messages, in characters. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `MESSAGE_COMPRESS_TRUNC` | `2000` | Characters of each message handed to the summariser. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CHAT_COMPACT_TOKENS` | about 80% of the window | Prompt tokens above which a conversation hands its older turns to memory. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CHAT_COMPACT_CHARS` | half the window | The same trigger in characters, used until the server has counted a request. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CHAT_COMPACT_MARGIN` | `4096` | Tokens kept free below the top of the window when that trigger is computed. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CHAT_KEEP_TURNS` | `3` | Most recent turns left in the conversation after it is compacted. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CHAT_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS` | `2000` | Characters of each model reply kept in the transcript memory is written from. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |

## Watchdogs

What stops a model that is repeating itself.

| Variable | Default | What it is | Read in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REASONING_LOOP_ENABLED` | `true` | Whether a reasoning that repeats itself is cut. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `REASONING_LOOP_WINDOW` | `200` | Characters of reasoning compared at a time. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `REASONING_LOOP_CHECK_EVERY` | `400` | Characters of reasoning between two comparisons. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `REASONING_LOOP_THRESHOLD` | `3` | Repetitions of the same passage that cut the reasoning. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `ACTION_LOOP_ENABLED` | `true` | Whether the same failing tool call, repeated, draws a warning to the agent. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `ACTION_LOOP_THRESHOLD` | `3` | Identical failing calls in a row before that warning. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `ERROR_RATE_WINDOW` | `5` | Recent tool calls looked at for a run of errors across different tools. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `ERROR_RATE_THRESHOLD` | `0.75` | Fraction of those that must have failed to draw the warning. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |

## What memory brings to a turn

| Variable | Default | What it is | Read in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CURATOR_ENABLED` | `true` | Whether a model call chooses what to recall. Off, the best keyword matches are used as they are. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CURATOR_CANDIDATES_EPISODES` | `10` | Episodes offered to that choice. *Project setting `CuratorEpisodes`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CURATOR_CANDIDATES_LEARNINGS` | `8` | Beliefs offered to that choice. *Project setting `CuratorLearnings`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CURATOR_CANDIDATES_RECENT` | `3` | Of the episodes offered, how many are simply the most recent. *Project setting `CuratorRecent`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CURATOR_MAX_FRAGMENTS` | `6` | Most fragments that may be placed in front of the agent for one turn. *Project setting `CuratorFragments`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `PRAGMA_EMBED_URL` | unset | Address of an embedding server, ending in `/v1`. With one, what is offered to that choice is found by meaning and not by the words it shares with the request. `/configure` sets one for the machine, and that one is used first; this is for a script. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `PRAGMA_EMBED_MODEL` | unset | The model name to ask that server for, when it hosts several. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `PRAGMA_EMBED_TIMEOUT` | `20` | Seconds an embedding call may take before the search goes by words instead. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CURATOR_OFFERED_EPISODES` | unset | `few`, `medium` or `many`: how many episodes are offered to that choice, said in a word. Set, it decides `CURATOR_CANDIDATES_EPISODES` and `CURATOR_CANDIDATES_RECENT`. `/settings` in a project sets it. *Project setting `RecallMemoriesOffered`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CURATOR_OFFERED_LEARNINGS` | unset | The same, for beliefs: set, it decides `CURATOR_CANDIDATES_LEARNINGS`. *Project setting `RecallBeliefsOffered`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CURATOR_TAKEN_EPISODES` | unset | `few`, `medium` or `many`: how readily episodes are taken from what was offered. Unset is `few`, and with both kinds at `few` recall is what it has always been. *Project setting `RecallMemoriesTaken`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CURATOR_TAKEN_LEARNINGS` | unset | The same, for beliefs. *Project setting `RecallBeliefsTaken`.* | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `MEMORY_NARRATIVE_CHARS` | `400` | Characters shown of what a recalled episode records. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `MEMORY_INTERPRETATION_CHARS` | `200` | Characters shown of what a recalled episode is taken to mean. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `EPISODES_RECALL_TOP_K` | `3` | Episodes returned when the choice above is switched off. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `LEARNINGS_RECALL_TOP_K` | `5` | Beliefs returned when the choice above is switched off. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `EPISODE_WORKSPACE_BOOST` | `2` | Advantage, in the keyword match, of an episode written in the folder being worked in. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |

## How memory is written and how it fades

| Variable | Default | What it is | Read in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SALIENCE_BASE` | `0.30` | Salience a new episode starts from. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `SALIENCE_SURPRISE_WEIGHT` | `0.12` | Added to it for each surprise the episode records. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `SALIENCE_IMPORTANCE_WEIGHT` | `0.40` | Weight of the episode's importance score in its starting salience. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `SALIENCE_CAP` | `0.95` | Upper bound of the starting salience. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `EPISODE_RECALL_BOOST` | `0.10` | How much being recalled strengthens an episode. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `EPISODE_RECALL_RULE` | `asymptotic` | `asymptotic` or `additive`: how that boost is applied. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `EPISODE_RECALL_PROCEDURAL_FACTOR` | `0.25` | Fraction of the boost earned by a recall made only to see how something is done. `1.0` treats every recall alike. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `EPISODE_IMPORTANCE_ANCHORS` | `5` | Stored episodes shown as a scale when a new one is scored. `0` shows none. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `EPISODE_DECAY_HALF_LIFE_DAYS` | `30` | Days for an episode's salience to halve when it is not recalled. `0` disables decay. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py), [`tools/mem_map.py`](../../tools/mem_map.py) |
| `EPISODE_DORMANT_THRESHOLD` | `0.15` | Salience below which an episode goes dormant. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py), [`tools/mem_map.py`](../../tools/mem_map.py) |
| `EPISODE_DELETE_AFTER_DAYS` | `0` | Days dormant before an episode nothing refers to is deleted. `0` never deletes. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `SEMANTIC_MIN_SOURCES` | `2` | Distinct episodes a new belief must rest on. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `SEMANTIC_CONFIRM_BONUS` | `0.1` | Confidence a belief gains each time it is confirmed. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `SEMANTIC_CONTRADICT_MALUS` | `0.2` | Confidence it loses each time it is contradicted. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `SEMANTIC_RETIRE_CONTRADICTIONS` | `2` | Contradictions after which a belief is retired. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `RECONSOLIDATION_ENABLED` | `true` | Whether later sessions may revise what earlier episodes and beliefs mean. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `RECONSOLIDATE_MAX_EPISODES` | `3` | Related past episodes re-read each time a session is written down. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `RECONSOLIDATE_REFORMULATE_AT` | same as `SEMANTIC_RETIRE_CONTRADICTIONS` | Contradictions after which a belief is reworded rather than retired. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `RECONSOLIDATE_BRIDGE_MIN_SOURCES` | `2` | Revised source episodes, in one session, that make a belief a candidate for rewording. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `AUTO_REFLECT` | `true` | Whether a reflection pass runs after a successful task. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `BATCH_SEGMENT` | unset | `1` has a batch run judged before it becomes an episode. Unset, every batch run with `--memory` writes one. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `MEMORY_SCHEMA` | `1` | `0` stops the memory faculties from asking the server to constrain their JSON. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |

## Optional faculties

Both are off unless turned on in `/configure`; the variables override that for one run.

| Variable | Default | What it is | Read in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SUGGEST_NEXT` | the choice made in `/configure` | `on` or `off`: whether the line you will probably type next is offered, in grey. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `SUGGEST_TIMEOUT` | `20` | Seconds after which that guess is given up on. | [`core/suggest.py`](../../core/suggest.py) |
| `CRITIC` | the choice made in `/configure` | `on` or `off`: whether a turn that changed something is checked against the request before the answer is delivered. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CRITIC_MAX_ROUNDS` | `2` | Times that check may send the same turn back. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `CRITIC_EVIDENCE_CHARS` | `24000` | Characters of the turn's record the check is shown. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |

## Where things are kept

| Variable | Default | What it is | Read in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PRAGMA_DATA_DIR` | `~/.pragma` | Folder holding the memory in use. The launcher sets it to the open project's own. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py), [`tools/mem_map.py`](../../tools/mem_map.py) |
| `LEARNINGS_PATH` | `learnings.json` in the data folder | File holding the beliefs. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `PRAGMA_PLUGINS` | `~/.pragma/plugins` | Folder the home screen reads plugins from. | [`tools/pragma_home.py`](../../tools/pragma_home.py) |

## Set by the launcher

Written for the conversation it starts. Listed so that nobody sets them by hand.

| Variable | Default | What it is | Read in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PRAGMA_PROJECT` | unset | Name of the open project. | [`agent/chat.py`](../../agent/chat.py) |
| `PRAGMA_WORKSPACE` | unset | Folder of the open project. A batch run uses it when `--cwd` is not given. | [`agent/batch.py`](../../agent/batch.py), [`agent/chat.py`](../../agent/chat.py) |
| `PRAGMA_REQUEST` | unset | File through which the conversation asks the launcher to do something on the way out. | [`agent/chat.py`](../../agent/chat.py) |
| `PRAGMA_SESSION_ID` | unset | Identifies a session, so that writing it down twice produces one episode. | [`core/skills/episode_consolidate/skill.py`](../../core/skills/episode_consolidate/skill.py) |
| `PRAGMA_ACCENT` | `178;132;255` | Accent colour of the screens, as `R;G;B`. | [`agent/chat.py`](../../agent/chat.py), [`agent/harness.py`](../../agent/harness.py), [`tools/mem_map.py`](../../tools/mem_map.py), [`tools/pragma_home.py`](../../tools/pragma_home.py), [`tools/pragma_menu.py`](../../tools/pragma_menu.py) |

## For development and tests

| Variable | Default | What it is | Read in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PRAGMA_DEBUG` | unset | `1` prints diagnostic output. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `PRAGMA_LOOK` | unset | `classic` draws a turn the way it was drawn before: the name of each tool, its arguments and its output. Unset, the turn is a ledger. | [`agent/chat.py`](../../agent/chat.py) |
| `PRAGMA_ALLOW_SELF_MODIFY` | unset | `true` lets a session write inside Pragma's own repository, which is otherwise refused. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
| `PRAGMA_CLOCK` | unset | Freezes the clock the memory reads at an ISO instant. | [`core/clock.py`](../../core/clock.py) |
| `PRAGMA_CLOCK_OFFSET` | unset | Shifts that clock by a number of seconds. | [`core/clock.py`](../../core/clock.py) |
| `PRAGMA_CONSOLIDATE_SYNC` | unset | `1` writes memory in the foreground on leaving, instead of in a background process. | [`agent/chat.py`](../../agent/chat.py) |
| `PRAGMA_CRITIC_SNAPSHOT` | unset | Folder that receives a copy of the workspace when a turn first delivers, for tests. | [`core/config.py`](../../core/config.py) |
